title: Golden spiral drawn inside nested squares

step.script: Start with a golden rectangle. Its long side divided by its short side equals phi, approximately one point six one eight.

primitives.meaning: Golden rectangle to subdivide into successively smaller squares

step.script: Remove the largest square. The remaining rectangle has the same proportions, rotated. Repeat to create smaller and smaller squares.

checkpoint.question: What happens to each successive square's side length?
checkpoint.expected_gist: It shrinks by a factor of one over phi, about 0.618.

step.script: Inside each square, draw a quarter-circle. Join their endpoints, turning in the same direction as the squares shrink.
These joined quarter-circles approximate a golden spiral. The exact spiral shrinks continuously by one over phi every quarter-turn.

primitives.meaning: Quarter-circle turn used in each successive square
